elements.name: Log Errors
elements.what: Record error details on a separate diagnostic channel (log file, console, trace buffer) at the point where the error occurs, instead of forcing all debug information through return values to the caller.
elements.problem: Callers need only actionable error information, but programmers debugging the system need full detail; funneling both through return codes bloats APIs and loses context available only at the error site.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 2 (Preschern 2022); also 'Patterns for Returning Error Information in C' (Preschern, EuroPLoP 2019, ACM DL)

elements.name: Lazy Cleanup
aka: let the OS reclaim at exit
elements.what: Deliberately never free dynamically allocated memory whose lifetime spans the whole program run, relying on the operating system to reclaim it at process exit.
elements.problem: Explicit deallocation of long-lived allocations adds code, ownership bookkeeping, and dangling-pointer risk for memory the process needs until it dies anyway; skipping the free removes that entire error class at the cost of unbounded-lifetime allocations.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 3, memory management patterns (Preschern 2022)
elements.borderline: distinct from Eternal Memory / static allocation (already in index under static-allocation): here memory IS dynamically allocated, only the cleanup is skipped

elements.name: Allocation Wrapper
elements.what: Wrap the raw allocation/deallocation calls (malloc/free) in your own functions so every allocation flows through one place that can check for failure, add statistics, tagging, debugging hooks, or alternative backing allocators.
elements.problem: Scattered direct malloc calls duplicate out-of-memory handling and make it impossible to instrument, audit, or retarget allocation behavior centrally.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 3, memory management patterns (Preschern 2022)

elements.name: Pointer Check
elements.what: Explicitly set pointers to an invalid value (NULL) when uninitialized or freed, and check pointers against that invalid value before dereferencing them.
elements.problem: Dangling and uninitialized pointers cause corruption far from the defect site; pairing deliberate invalidation with checks before use converts silent memory corruption into detectable, handleable conditions.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 3, memory management patterns (Preschern 2022)
elements.borderline: overlaps sanity-check and complete-parameter-checking in the index; kept separate because the mechanism is the invalidate-on-free/init + check-before-use pairing specific to raw-pointer lifetime, not general input validation

elements.name: Function Control
elements.what: Add a data parameter (enum, flag, mode value) to a function that selects which of several behaviors the function performs, letting one API entry point cover a family of variants without passing function pointers.
elements.problem: An API needs caller-selectable behavior variation but a full callback/dynamic interface is overkill; a control parameter keeps the interface small at the cost of coupling the caller to a behavior selector.
elements.borderline: API-shape mechanism near the syntax floor; the same construct is cataloged as the 'flag argument' smell by Fowler - included as the named Fluent C mechanism with that tension recorded

elements.name: Stateless Software-Module
elements.what: Provide a set of logically related functions that keep no state between calls: every resource a function needs is acquired and released inside the call, so the caller owns nothing and calls are independent.
elements.problem: Callers should not have to reason about initialization order, ownership, or hidden coupling between calls; making the module stateless eliminates those questions at the cost of ruling out cross-call caching or context.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 5, 'Data Lifetime and Ownership' (Preschern 2022); also Preschern, 'C Patterns on Data Lifetime and Ownership' (PLoP paper)
elements.borderline: module-structure decision close to a design principle, but named as a discrete pattern with a concrete C realization in two published sources

elements.name: Software-Module with Global State
elements.what: Implement a module whose related functions operate on shared file-scope (static global) state inside the module, with initialization/cleanup functions for that state, while callers hold no instance at all.
elements.problem: Functions need common prepared resources (buffers, connections, config) but callers should not manage per-caller instances; one module-internal state blob serves all callers, trading simplicity for a single shared context.
elements.named_in: Fluent C ch. 5, 'Data Lifetime and Ownership' (Preschern 2022); also Preschern, 'C Patterns on Data Lifetime and Ownership' (PLoP paper)
elements.borderline: sits near Singleton/Monostate (both in index) but is the instance-less C module form, named in its own right; do not fold - no object identity or class is involved

parked_architecture.name: Safety Executive
parked_architecture.why: Douglass safety pattern cataloged in Preschern/Kajtazovic/Kreiner 'Building a Safety Architecture Pattern System' (EuroPLoP 2013, ACM 10.1145/2739011.2739028): a centralized safety monitor component coordinating fail-safe shutdown across subsystems - system-level structure, fails the altitude test upward.

parked_architecture.name: Monitor-Actuator (channel pair)
parked_architecture.why: Douglass safety pattern in the same Preschern EuroPLoP 2013 safety pattern system: separate actuation channel and monitoring channel as distinct components - architecture-level channel structure (index's dual-channel and protected-single-channel cover the in-component mechanisms).

parked_architecture.name: Safety tactics catalog (Wu-Kelly, via Preschern's GSN tactic analysis)
parked_architecture.why: Preschern's EuroPLoP 2013/2019 safety-pattern-system papers organize patterns under safety tactics (condition monitoring, degradation, replication/diversity redundancy, repair...) - tactics are Phase 3 architecture-realm material; the implementable members (sanity check, watchdog, N-version, dual channel) are already in the design index.
